          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2). Before the failure is decided, findings.md is restored outright: every post-run check, cheap\n    or full, reads the runner's file, an edit alone fails nothing, and a completed attempt that edited\n    it carries a quoted restore notice under its audit line (spec, criteria 8 and 9).\n\n    A verb that passes `retain_answer` keeps every attempt's full answer: right at the model-return\n    boundary, before any HEAD check, verification or answer check can stop the run, the protected\n    answer is saved as local evidence and its location joins the attempt's diagnostics - the parser's\n    rejections, the call and verify failures included - and is printed on success (bead\n    coding-harness-hgvp). A failed call keeps the output it returned.\n\n    A verb that passes `protect_lifecycle` snapshots the change's lifecycle fields (`status`,\n    `implementation_status`) in spec, optional design and plan right before every call. \"\n                \"its destination cannot be assessed and the call does not start.\"\n            )\n        (agent / \"models-store.json\").write_text(json.dumps(store), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        _dropped, notices = activate_overlay(agent, store, policy)\n        retain_address_notices(notices)\n        for notice in notices:\n            print(f\"Address notice: {notice}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        home = scratch / \"home\"\n        home.mkdir()\n        check_overlay(agent, home, model, policy=policy)\n        row = stage2_go.definition_of(store, stage2_go.PROVIDER, model)\n        if row is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"the refreshed definitions of {model} are missing or duplicated;           "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::dispatch_go",
          "end_line": 2391,
          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses. A same-host path move is announced\n    here once more; a foreign destination is refused before the send. The\n    caller supplies the models.json or checked-model.json that its launch\n    consumes; its selected API and explicit base must match the assessment.\n    \"\"\"\n    if destination is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"the launch of {model} carries no checked destination; no model request starts.\")\n    try:\n        policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(root)\n    except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n    verdict = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, destination)\n    if verdict.notice:\n        retain_address_notices([verdict.notice])\n        print(f\"Address notice: {verdict.notice}\")\n    if verdict.problem:\n        raise Refused(verdict.problem)\n    entry = endpoint_entry(root)\n    paid = model in (entry.get(\"modelle\") or []) or model in (entry.get(\"modelle_terms\") or {})\n    if paid or admission is None:\n        warnings = terms_warnings({**entry, \"modelle\": [model]})\n        retain_terms_warnings(warnings)\n        for warning in warnings:\n            print(f\"Terms warning: {warning}\")\n        problem = terms_problem(entry, model)\n    else:\n        problem = admission(root, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    # Check the artifact Pi actually consumes, not just the caller's earlier assessment.\n    # Never echo its contents: a mismatched URL can carry credentials.\n    try:\n        if configuration is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing configuration\")\n        content = json.loads(Path(configuration).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        if Path(configuration).name == \"checked-model.json\":\n            actual = content.get(\"model\") if content.get(\"provider\") == OPENCODE else None\n        else:\n            actual = stage2_go.definition_of(content.get(\"providers\"), OPENCODE, model)\n        if not isinstance(actual, dict) or actual.get(\"id\") != model:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing or ambiguous model\")\n        if any(actual.get(field) != verdict.definition.get(field) for field in (\"api\", \"baseUrl\")):\n            raise ValueError(\"destination mismatch\")\n        checked = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, actual)\n        if not checked.admitted:\n            raise ValueError(\"refused destination\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"the sending configuration of {model} does not match its checked destination; no request starts.\"\n        ) from None\n    return send(*args, **kwargs)\n",

          "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    # The class statement and the current spec review (bead coding-harness-ttic): one admission\n    # for every route, checked before a model starts; a spike reaches the existing checks.\n    admission = review_admission(root, change)\n    if admission.class_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.class_problem)\n    if admission.review_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.review_problem)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2). A failed call keeps the output it returned.\n\n    A verb that passes `protect_lifecycle` snapshots the change's lifecycle fields (`status`,\n    `implementation_status`) in spec, optional design and plan right before every call.           "end_line": 7387,
          "excerpt": "def run_work_model(\n    ctx: Context,\n    prompt: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    writable: bool,\n    key: str | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One non-interactive Claude Code work call with file tools only.\"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        prompt_file = Path(tmp) / \"work-prompt.md\"\n        prompt_file.write_text(prompt, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        command = [\n            \"claude\",\n            \"-p\",\n            f\"Run the phase for {ctx.change} exactly as the appended instructions say.\",\n            \"--append-system-prompt-file\",\n            str(prompt_file),\n            \"--model\",\n            endpoint[1],\n        ]\n        if endpoint[2]:\n            command += [\"--effort\", endpoint[2]]\n        command += [\n            \"--tools\",\n            WORK_WRITE_TOOLS if writable else WORK_READ_TOOLS,\n            \"--restricted\",\n            \"--safe-mode\",\n            \"--strict-mcp-config\",\n            \"--permission-mode\",\n            \"acceptEdits\" if writable else \"dontAsk\",\n            \"--permission-prompts\",\n            \"none\",\n            \"--no-session-persistence\",\n            \"--output-format\",\n            \"text\",\n        ]\n        if key is None:\n            env = foreign_env({})\n        else:\n            config_dir = Path(tmp) / \"claude-config\"\n            config_dir.mkdir()\n            env = glm_env(key, config_dir, endpoint[1])\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, env, key, timeout=timeout, limit=limit)\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        error = fail(\"claude\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\", key)\n        # A failed call's printed answer travels along for the repair evidence; nothing else changes.\n        error.partial_answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n        raise error\n    answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n    if not answer.strip():\n        raise fail(\"claude\", done, \"the answer is empty\", key)\n    return answer\n",

          "excerpt": "def repair_prompt(\n    ctx: Context,\n    baseline: str,\n    taken: list[tuple[str, list[str]]],\n    diagnostics: list[str],\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None] = CODEX,\n    inputs: dict[Path, bytes] | None = None,\n    held_rows: list[tuple[str, list[str], list[str]]] | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The implement contract with the repair block: the format, the must-runs, the baseline, the rows.\"\"\"\n    rows = \"\\n\".join(f\"- {row[0]} [{row[1]}, {row[2]}] {row[4]}: {row[5]} — Status: {row[7]}\" for _, row in taken)\n    spec = prompt_input(ctx.folder / \"spec.md\", inputs)\n    plan = prompt_input(ctx.plan, inputs)\n    extra = [\n        REPAIR_FORMAT if endpoint == CODEX else REPAIR_FORMAT_FILE_TOOLS,\n        # A command-capable Codex runs the must-runs itself; the file-tools route delegates the same\n        # checks to the runner. The references come from the accepted plan's cached snapshot, so a retry rereads\n        # nothing the attempt may have edited (spec, criteria 13, 14 and 16).\n        \"## Must-run checks before handback\\n\\n\"\n        + (MUST_RUN_COMMANDS if endpoint == CODEX else MUST_RUN_DELEGATED_REPAIR)\n        + \"\\n\\nLedger tests:\\n\"\n        + repair_must_run_refs(ctx.root, plan.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        f\"Repair baseline: {baseline}\",\n        f\"## Taken rows\\n\\n{rows}\",\n        f\"## Accepted spec\\n\\n{spec}\",\n        f\"## Accepted plan\\n\\n{plan}\",\n    ]\n    if held_rows:\n        # The model is told the held rows are not its work (spec, criterion 18); the rows stay\n        # readable in the findings record it already receives.\n        ids = \", \".join(row[0] for _, row, _ in held_rows)\n        extra.append(\n            \"## Held rows — not your work\\n\\n\"\n            f\"The runner handed {ids} to the orchestrator before your call: each row's `Where` names \"\n            \"a path the runner does not commit. They are not your work: do not repair, answer or \"\n            \"book them, and answer only the taken rows above.\"\n        )\n    if diagnostics:\n        extra.append(\"## Earlier post-run diagnostics\\n\\n\" + \"\\n\\n\".join(diagnostics))\n    return work_prompt(ctx.root, \"04-implement.md\", ctx.change, \"\\n\\n\".join(extra), inputs)\n",

          "excerpt": "def preflight(\n    root: Path,\n    change: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    bead_file: str = \"spec.md\",\n    required: tuple[str, ...] = (),\n    admission_problem: Callable[[Path, str], str | None] | None = None,\n) -> Context:\n    \"\"\"The refusals that precede everything else: change, artefacts and declaration.\n\n    `admission_problem` replaces the individual declaration for the free class:\n    it receives the root and the model id and returns a problem or None (ADR\n    0021, decision 3). Every other call keeps the strict declaration.\n    \"\"\"\n    folder = folder_of(root, change)\n    bead = _artefact_bead(folder / bead_file)\n    if bead is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"plans/changes/{change}/{bead_file} has no bead in its header; the runner cannot name the work.\")\n    for name in required:\n        path = folder / name\n        try:\n            path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n            raise Refused(f\"plans/changes/{change}/{name} cannot be read.\") from error\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    return Context(root, change, folder, bead, go_admission=admission_problem)\n",

          "excerpt": "def begin_work_call(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    prompt: str,\n    attempt: int,\n    route: str,\n    destination: Path,\n    reason: str | None = None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Check and record one explore/implement attempt in its phase artefact.\"\"\"\n    result = checked_prompt(ctx, endpoint, prompt)\n    if destination == ctx.findings and not destination.exists():\n        destination.write_text(findings_header(ctx, producer_for(endpoint)), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    why = f\" · reason {reason}\" if reason else \"\"\n    append(\n        destination,\n        f\"Stage-2 call, {today()}: {verb} · attempt {attempt} · route {route} · \"\n        f\"endpoint {endpoint[0]} · model {endpoint[1]}{why} · leak check clean over \"\n        f\"{result.files} files, {result.commits} commits, {result.rules} rules.\",\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_fallback_review(\n    ctx: Context, config: dict, opus_failure: CallFailed\n) -> tuple[bytes, str, list[list[str]], str, tuple[str, str, str | None], object]:\n    \"\"\"The declared fallback review through Pi, after the Opus route failed twice (spec criteria 13-15).\n\n    The leak check runs first and a BLOCK still refuses - no fallback call starts. The\n    fallback reads the spec body fresh at its own call start, and the body on disk must still\n    be those bytes when the call ends. A failed or unreadable fallback fails the whole call.\n    \"\"\"\n    if config[\"fallback_model\"] is None:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the Opus review produced no readable review ({opus_failure}); no fallback model is declared \"\n            \"in model-endpoints.yaml's `spec_review` block, so no fallback call starts.\"\n        )\n    endpoint = (str(config[\"fallback_endpoint\"]), str(config[\"fallback_model\"]), None)\n    if endpoint[0] != OPENCODE:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the spec review's fallback endpoint must be {OPENCODE}, where the runner's Pi reviews; \"\n            f\"{endpoint[0]} is not.\"\n        )\n    problem = terms_problem(endpoint_entry(ctx.root), endpoint[1])\n    if problem is not None:\n        raise CallFailed(f\"the fallback review is not admitted on its declared terms: {problem}\")\n    require_committed_review_spec(ctx.root, ctx.change)\n    commit = _git_output(ctx.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    body = spec_body_bytes(ctx.folder / \"spec.md\")\n    if body != spec_body_of(_git_bytes(ctx.root, \"show\", f\"{commit}:plans/changes/{ctx.change}/spec.md\")):\n        raise CallFailed(\"the spec changed while the review snapshot was read.\")\n    prompt = spec_review_prompt(ctx.root, ctx.change, body)\n    result = checked_prompt(ctx, endpoint, prompt)\n    require_pi()\n    discovery = discover_free(ctx.root, allow_empty=True)\n    ctx.models_store = discovery.get(\"models_store\")\n    require_committed_review_spec(ctx.root, ctx.change)\n    try:\n        answer = run_reviewer(\n            ctx,\n            endpoint[1],\n            prompt,\n            reviewer_key(),\n            free=False,\n            timeout_seconds=int(config[\"timeout_seconds\"]),\n        )\n    except CallFailed as error:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the Opus review produced no readable review ({opus_failure}) and the fallback review \"\n            f\"failed too ({error}).\"\n        ) from error\n    rows = readable_review(answer)\n    if spec_body_bytes(ctx.folder / \"spec.md\") != body:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            \"the spec body changed during the fallback review; no block is written for bytes the reviewer did not read.\"\n        )\n    return body, commit, rows, answer, endpoint, result\n",

          "excerpt": "def dispatch_go(\n    root: Path, model: str, send: Callable, *args, admission=None, destination=None, configuration=None, **kwargs\n):\n    \"\"\"The final shared Go send boundary, independent of tools, retries and saved admission.\n\n    Only a caller's checked discovered-free admission can replace paid terms.\n    A declared paid record always keeps its terms check, even with that callback.\n    All command construction and leak scans precede this function.\n\n    `destination` is the caller's checked effective definition. The boundary\n    re-assesses it against the address policy read fresh from the held\n    declaration (criterion 6): an earlier selection, a saved overlay, a\n    receipt, a resumed round, a replacement or a retry never dispatches a\n    destination the current record refuses. A same-host path move is announced\n    here once more; a foreign destination is refused before the send. The\n    caller supplies the models.json or checked-model.json that its launch\n    consumes; its selected API and explicit base must match the assessment.\n    \"\"\"\n    if destination is None:\n        raise Refused(f\"the launch of {model} carries no checked destination; no model request starts.\")\n    try:\n        policy = stage2_go.load_address_policy(root)\n    except stage2_go.RecordUnusable as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the Go address record is unusable: {error}\") from None\n    verdict = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, destination)\n    if verdict.notice:\n        retain_address_notices([verdict.notice])\n        print(f\"Address notice: {verdict.notice}\")\n    if verdict.problem:\n        raise Refused(verdict.problem)\n    entry = endpoint_entry(root)\n    paid = model in (entry.get(\"modelle\") or []) or model in (entry.get(\"modelle_terms\") or {})\n    if paid or admission is None:\n        warnings = terms_warnings({**entry, \"modelle\": [model]})\n        retain_terms_warnings(warnings)\n        for warning in warnings:\n            print(f\"Terms warning: {warning}\")\n        problem = terms_problem(entry, model)\n    else:\n        problem = admission(root, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    # Check the artifact Pi actually consumes, not just the caller's earlier assessment.\n    # Never echo its contents: a mismatched URL can carry credentials.\n    try:\n        if configuration is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing configuration\")\n        content = json.loads(Path(configuration).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        if Path(configuration).name == \"checked-model.json\":\n            actual = content.get(\"model\") if content.get(\"provider\") == OPENCODE else None\n        else:\n            actual = stage2_go.definition_of(content.get(\"providers\"), OPENCODE, model)\n        if not isinstance(actual, dict) or actual.get(\"id\") != model:\n            raise ValueError(\"missing or ambiguous model\")\n        if any(actual.get(field) != verdict.definition.get(field) for field in (\"api\", \"baseUrl\")):\n            raise ValueError(\"destination mismatch\")\n        checked = stage2_go.assess(policy, model, actual)\n        if not checked.admitted:\n            raise ValueError(\"refused destination\")\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"the sending configuration of {model} does not match its checked destination; no request starts.\"\n        ) from None\n    return send(*args, **kwargs)\n",

          "excerpt": "def cli_argv(transport: str, root: Path, cli: str, model: str, prompt: str, extension: Path | None = None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The one interactive form per transport: no headless verb, no fallback, no extra writable directory.\n\n    The prompt can begin with `---` (a handover's frontmatter) or with a word that is a subcommand. Codex\n    and Pi get it after `--`, the end of their options. Pi reads a prompt that starts with `@` as a file name,\n    which is why `run` refuses such a prompt; Pi has no print or RPC mode here, so the window stays interactive.\n    \"\"\"\n    if transport == \"codex\":\n        return [\n            cli,\n            \"--no-daemon\",\n            \"--model\",\n            model,\n            \"--cd\",\n            str(root),\n            \"--sandbox\",\n            \"workspace-write\",\n            \"--ask-for-approval\",\n            \"on-request\",\n            \"--\",\n            prompt,\n        ]\n    # Discovery is off like in the reviewer call (spec criterion 11): no MCP servers (an MCP file tool would\n    # bypass the policy's worktree bounds), skills, prompt templates or themes. Context files stay on, so the\n    # session reads the repository's AGENTS.md (maintainer, 2026-10-09).\n    return [\n        cli,\n        \"--no-extensions\",\n        \"--no-mcp\",\n        \"--no-skills\",\n        \"--no-prompt-templates\",\n        \"--no-themes\",\n        \"-e\",\n        str(extension),\n        \"--offline\",\n        \"--no-approve\",\n        \"--model\",\n        model,\n        \"--\",\n        prompt,\n    ]\n",

          "excerpt": "def install_policy(private: Path, runner) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Copy the extension into the session's private directory; the copy, not the source, is what Pi loads.\n\n    The extension refuses writes to its own file, and a copy under `.stage2-sessions/` is one the session's\n    file tools may not touch either, whereas `scripts/` holds a tracked file of the worktree.\n    \"\"\"\n    copy = private / POLICY_FILE\n    try:\n        shutil.copyfile(POLICY_SOURCE, copy)\n    except OSError as error:\n        raise runner.Refused(f\"the policy extension {POLICY_SOURCE.name} could not be copied: {error}\") from error\n    return copy\n",

          "excerpt": "def require_pi() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Refuse unless the repository wrapper prints exactly the pinned version (spec, criterion 27).\n\n    The wrapper is the one path to Pi (ADR 0019): it refuses a missing,\n    mismatched or unusable local install before any model request, and this\n    check ties its answer to the manifest pin. Runs before the prompt check,\n    the call line and any call, in a scratch directory with no key: a Pi off\n    the pin sends nothing. The session verb calls it after its argument and\n    handover checks.\n    \"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        env = foreign_env({\"HOME\": tmp, \"PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR\": tmp})\n        try:\n            done = launch(\n                [str(PI_WRAPPER), \"--version\"],\n                Path(tmp),\n                env,\n                timeout=PI_VERSION_SECONDS,\n                limit=f\"the version check's limit of {PI_VERSION_SECONDS} seconds\",\n            )\n        except CallFailed as error:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"{PI_WRAPPER} could not be checked ({error}); it is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; no call starts.\"\n            ) from None\n    said = (done.stdout or \"\").strip()\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        # The wrapper's own refusal names the defect; its last lines travel with this one.\n        tail = \"\\n\".join((done.stderr or \"\").splitlines()[-5:])\n        detail = f\": {tail}\" if tail else \"\"\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"{PI_WRAPPER} --version ended {done.returncode}; it is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; \"\n            f\"no call starts{detail}.\"\n        )\n    if said != PI_VERSION:\n        raise Refused(f\"pi {said or 'printed nothing'} is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; no call starts.\")\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "require_pi",
          "start_line": 3272,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },

          "end_line": 7827,
          "excerpt": "def test_a_pi_off_the_pin_is_refused(\n    world: World, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str], verb: str, fault: dict | str\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 27: a Pi that is not exactly the pinned version starts no leak check, no call line and no call.\"\"\"\n    manifest = json.loads((REPO_ROOT / \"tools\" / \"pi\" / \"package.json\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    assert manifest[\"dependencies\"][\"@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent\"] == stage2.PI_VERSION, (\n        \"the runner's pin must be the manifest's, not a literal of its own\"\n    )\n    monkeypatch.setattr(stage2, \"PI_VERSION_SECONDS\", 0.5)\n    programs = None\n    steps = {\"pi\": [{\"stdout\": rows(1)}] * 3}\n    if fault == \"absent\":\n        (world.bin / \"pin-pi\").unlink()\n        world.script(**steps)\n    elif fault == \"too-slow\":\n        # A probe past the pin limit is stopped at the injected expiry, never waited out on the\n        # machine: the doubled communicate raises what a hung wrapper would have caused.\n        clock = FakeClock(monkeypatch, UTC_START)\n        version_argv = [str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), \"--version\"]\n        plans = [(lambda command: command == version_argv, {\"duration\": 30.0})]\n        programs = ScriptedPrograms(monkeypatch, clock, plans)\n        world.script(**steps)\n    else:\n        world.script(**steps, **fault)\n    assert world.run(verb) == 2, \"a Pi off the pin must refuse with exit 2\"\n    if programs is not None:\n        (handed,) = programs.waits([str(stage2.PI_WRAPPER), \"--version\"])\n        assert handed[\"timeout\"] == 0.5 and handed[\"outcome\"] == \"timeout\", handed\n    assert world.calls() == [], \"a call started\"\n    assert not world.record().exists()\n    text = world.text() if world.findings.exists() else \"\"\n    assert text.count(\"Stage-2 call,\") <= 1, \"a call line was written\"\n    assert \"leak check\" not in capsys.readouterr().out.lower(), \"the leak check ran before the pin\"\n",

          "excerpt": "## The workflow in one screen\n\n| # | Phase | Artifact | Gate |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Explore | `plans/changes/<name>/research.md` | — |\n| 1a | Interview | `decisions.md` | the class minimums met — feature ≥ 3 · ADR change ≥ 5 (feature with ADR: 5 total) · spike 3 topics or reasoned skip · bounded 1 or reasoned skip — gate `interview-minimums` |\n| 2 | Spec | `spec.md` | validator green, no open `[DECISION]` |\n| 2a | Spec-Review *(not for a spike)* | lines for `findings.md`, dimension SPEC | a current review of the spec, no open `[AMBIGUITY]`; at most three spec-review rounds — the final draft after round three needs no new review, a fourth round only by a recorded maintainer answer |\n| 2b | Design *(by class)* | `design.md` | validator green; an ADR draft when `architectural` |\n| 3 | Plan | `plan.md` | validator green |\n| 4 | Implement | code + tests | `make verify` green |\n| 4b | Review loop *(stage 2)* | loop rows, into `findings.md` after the phase-6 verdict | rounds until a clean round — the free swarm, the Flash swarm, then the paid ladder (ADR 0021); a targeted check after each runner repair and each orchestrator hand repair, the full `make verify` before phase 6 |\n| 5 | Verify | test output as evidence | stop-hook blocks on a red tree |\n| 6 | Review | `findings.md` | no open BLOCKER — `[DIVERGENT]` counts as BLOCKER |\n| 7 | Commit | pull request | CI green |\n\n**Stage 2** (framework content, ADR 0007 as amended by ADR 0011 and ADR 0016): a foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py`, which runs the leak check before every call. Codex drafts spec, design and plan (`draft <change>`; GLM 5.3 after two failed attempts) and reviews 6; Opus 5.5 reviews 2a (`spec-review <change>`); the review loop (4b) runs on OpenCode Go through Pi until a clean round (ADR 0021): round 1 is the free swarm, the models the `free_stage` rule selects from a forced live catalog refresh, on the implementation diff alone with no tools; round 2 is the Flash swarm, up to three cheapest reachable admitted paid models in parallel; then one id of the `opencode-go` entry's `modelle` set per round, cheapest first: the runner orders it by the declared `anfragen_5h` (requests per 5 hours, more is cheaper); a failed Flash member is replaced by the cheapest unconsumed one. Amends no decision and supersedes no ADR.\n* Review: the maintainer's answers of 2026-10-12 in the interview of change\n  adr-owning-change, recorded as Q-1 to Q-5 in\n  `plans/changes/adr-owning-change/decisions.md` — the change claims its ADR\n  files in its own spec header (Q-1); an ADR edit no change claims is a\n  finding, and the inference from the diff goes (Q-2); this rule gets an ADR\n  and the gate travels with the kit, \"Das soll auch reisen, beides\" (Q-3);\n  the whole gate travels, with a day per repository (Q-4); answer and claimed\n  files agree in both directions (Q-5) — and the answer \"yes\" to the ADR\n  question (`decisions/answers/adr-owning-change/adr.yaml`) · the acceptance\n  is the merge commit and is written nowhere else, so the header's `review`\n  stays empty (ADR 0008) · Decider: maintainer · prepared by a Claude Code\n  session\n* Date: 2026-10-13 · takes effect on merge\n\n## Context\n\n* **The interview gate infers an ADR's owner from the diff.** Every change\n  folder with a file in the measured diff owns an ADR the diff changes, and\n  exactly one must (`scripts/check_interview_minimums.py`, read at `2d6a1c6`).\n  The duty behind it is the maintainer's of 2026-10-08: creating or changing\n  an ADR owes five interview answers, whatever the change's class\n  (`plans/changes/archive/2026-10-08-interview-minimums/decisions.md`).\n* **The inference fails on cross-folder work.** Change criterion-test-ledger\n  (bead coding-harness-909) adds ADR 0013 and migrates the plans of four other\n  changes; the gate went red, and the change repaired it with an interim rule:\n  a folder touched through `plan.md` alone is no owner, and beside another\n  owner the ADR's text decides (pull request #126, read at `7f53552`). Any\n  other cross-folder edit breaks that rule again.\n* **Nothing states an owner.** `owner:` in an ADR header names a role, never\n  a change (`provenance.yaml`, the roles block). An answer file binds a change\n  to its answer, never an ADR to a change, and its format (`schema_version:\n  1`) is shared with LakeSwitch and frozen \"not now\"\n  (`docs/research/2026-10-11-adr-answer-pin-plan.md`).\n* **A \"yes\" is not followed up.** `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §2 said: \"Nothing checks\n  … that a 'yes' is followed by an ADR.\"\n* **The gate does not travel.** The gate list that runs it travels with the\n  kit, the script does not, and its cut-off is a constant holding this\n  repository's day, 2026-10-08 (`scripts/kit/manifest.yaml`, read at\n  `2d6a1c6`). A reader of the ADR\n  sees it, but an ADR has one header for every edit, so an amendment must\n  rewrite it, and `owner:` there already names a role.\n* (3) **In the answer file**, as a key listing the ADR paths.           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included. The prompts ask them\n   to read nothing outside the worktree and the repository's git directory — a\n   request, not a lock, and the doctrine says so in those words. The\n   maintainer accepted this as a residual risk on 2026-09-30, choosing it over\n   a proof of about one hour's work, for the reviewers. Explore and implement\n   widen what is read and add writes; whether that acceptance reaches them is\n   for the maintainer to confirm by merging this pull request.\n5. **Explore and implement run on GLM 5.3 Flash — decided, not built.** They\n   run there for every change, whatever its class: the class is stated in the\n   spec, after exploration. The runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) has no verb for\n   either phase yet, no plan marking assigns a step to Flash, and no effort is\n   set for it. Until that is built, `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3 runs the two phases:\n   Haiku 4.5 explores and Sonnet 5.5 implements. This is an open item of the\n   change, not a claim that it works.\n6. **Endpoints are architecture; the models on them are declaration\n   (amended on 2026-10-30).** Which endpoints framework content may reach\n   stays this ADR's matter (decision 2) and its amendments'. Which models run\n   on a declared endpoint is set by `model-endpoints.yaml` alone, each through\n   a dated data-terms reading that the runner checks before every call.\n   Admitting, marking, removing or excluding a model there is a decision pull\n   request on that `human-decided` file, never an amendment of this ADR: the\n   OpenCode Go catalog changes too often to be architecture. A newly admitted\n   model takes a place in the review loop's ladder only; any other role\n   (explore, implem",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **Framework content may also go to `opencode-go`** — at\n   `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`, through Pi\n   (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, at the version the runner pins), with\n   the three ids below. Of the stage-2 phases, the review loop (4b) only,\n   with the runner's `probe` that measures its rungs. The\n   sentence of ADR 0007 decision 2 that closes with \"Nothing else goes, and\n   nowhere else\" now closes with Codex, Z.ai's GLM and OpenCode Go; nothing\n   else goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to none of the\n   three. The interactive `session` verb reaches a declared endpoint under\n   its own amendment (bead coding-harness-amp); this declaration is what that\n   verb waits for before it opens its OpenCode path to the three ids.\n2. **The loop's reviewer role moves.** The loop leaves GLM for the ladder;\n   the spec review and the review stay with Codex exactly as ADR 0007 set\n   them (the maintainer, 2026-10-08), and phase 6 keeps resuming the\n   phase-2a session. Codex and GLM remain declared endpoints for what still\n   routes to them — explore and implement stay on GLM 5.3 Flash.\n3. **The ladder is data, not code.** Round *n* of the loop calls\n   `modelle[n-1]` of the `opencode-go` entry (the order at this decision;\n   the yaml is the truth and no doctrine text repeats it): round 1\n   `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, round 2 `mimo-v2.6-flash`, round 3\n   `mimo-v2.6-pro`. Rounds 1 and 2 both run, each still held by an undecided\n   row; round 3 starts only when round 2 wrote at least one row whose status\n   begins `taken`. The loop runs at most three rounds. Reordering the list is\n   a one-line pull request that touches `model-endpoints.yaml` and nothing\n   else.\n4. **The unconfined reads accepted for ADR 0007's reviewers extend to the\n   rungs — measured, not assumed.** A round has `read`, `grep`, `find` and\n   `ls` and nothing that writes or runs a command; but `read` reaches files\n   outside the worktree, and Pi has no switch that confines it. A rung can\n   therefore read what the maintainer's user can read — the secrets file and\n   the customer instance's checkout included — and send it to OpenCode Go.\n   What bounds it is the prompt's request to read nothing outside the\n   worktree and the repository's git directory: a request, not a lock. The\n   leak check scans what this repository presents, not what a rung reads.\n   The maintainer accepted this residual risk for reviewers on 2026-09-30;\n   it reaches the three rungs by this record.\n5. **The key stays in the runner.** It is read from the secrets file at call\n   time, reaches the call only in its environment as `OPENCODE_API_KEY`,\n   never appears in an argument or in a file the runner writes, and an\n   OpenCode Go call carries no other endpoint's key.\n6. **Each round is isolated, and Pi is pinned.** Each call gets a fresh,\n   empty Pi configuration directory whose one file switches Pi's own retries\n   off, a scratch home directory, and the switches that keep extensions, MCP\n   servers, skills, context files, prompt templates, themes, project trust,\n   sessions and every network request but the model call off. The isolation\n   was measured on Pi 1.1.0; the runner refuses any other version, and\n   raising the pin means measuring it again. The effort is Pi's `max`, which\n   Pi clamps to each model's ceiling — `max` for DeepSeek, `high` for both\n   MiMo rungs: a known limit, not a failure.\n7. **The address is measured before anything builds on it.** Three calls,\n   one per rung, run through the runner and Pi in phase 4 of the change that\n   carries this record — declaration and leak check in front of each, as one\n   special run whose commits are named in the pull request body. After the\n   probe, the change's own review loop runs on the ladder, at most three\n   rounds.           "citation": "docs/adr/0017-codex-repairs-taken-findings.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 120,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Codex repairs both kinds, with a fresh Codex re-check\",\nbecause it implements the maintainer's model choice without weakening the\nrepair evidence contract.\n\n1. **Codex repairs all taken findings in one batch** through `python3\n   scripts/stage2.py repair <change>`: loop-record rows, released loop rows\n   and phase-6 findings. Each Codex attempt starts `gpt-6.1-sol` at effort\n   `max` in a fresh session, with the existing `workspace-write` configuration,\n   hooks and memories off, and no added directory, automatic approval or\n   bypass. Repair reads no GLM key and never routes to `glm-coding-plan`.\n2. **Only post-run failures advance the chain:** Codex; a fresh Codex attempt\n   with the first attempt's diagnostics; Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` on\n   Stage 1 with both diagnostics. A model call failure stops; with unchanged\n   HEAD, the existing restoration returns the worktree to baseline. When\n   Codex is unavailable, the orchestrator deliberately starts\n   `--stage2-off <reason>`, which uses Sonnet alone and records why. A\n   declaration refusal or leak-check BLOCK stops without fallback.\n3. **The orchestrator decides, the verb repairs, the reviewer re-checks.**\n   The orchestrator writes `taken — <reason>` or `rejected — <reason>`, or\n   takes a finding no test can show as `taken — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Repair keeps those inputs, requests one fixed line per row and a measured\n   time entry, and starts no review. The runner checks each exact prompt,\n   prepares and formats the result, runs `make verify`, checks the time and\n   evidence, writes statuses and makes one clean descendant checkpoint.\n   A Codex call that moves HEAD stops before restoration or a runner commit.\n4. **The existing proof and statuses stand.** A code finding requires a\n   defined test the runner demonstrates red against baseline code; a finding\n   taken as `not a test` is proven by the separate re-check. Fixed rows read\n   `fixed — tests/<path>::<function>` or `fixed — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Failed attempts retain their audit, quoted diagnostics and changed-file\n   evidence, while their model-written statuses are restored. Private loop\n   rows are marked only after the checkpoint; unreleased rows reach the\n   repair in the prompt rather than a worktree file.\n5. **The same model may repair phase-6 findings; a fresh session re-checks.**\n   A phase-6 verdict after an earlier `## Phase 6` block in `findings.md` — a\n   re-check — runs Codex read-only without resuming the repair, a prior\n   verdict or a historical phase-2a session; the first phase-6 review keeps\n   the resume rule of ADR 0016. Loop marks may\n   resume only that new verdict thread after its verdict. This replaces ADR\n   0015's blanket reviewer/repairer separation; it does not give review calls\n   write tools or move any review to another model.\n6. **The loop budget and run count stand.** A fixed row counts as taken;\n   round 3 requires a taken or fixed row in round 2, and the maximum stays\n   three rounds. The orchestrator writes `Broke a test` from the repair\n   evidence before the next round or release. Audit lines and historical GLM\n   counts retain their format. Initial implementation, Explore and draft's\n   GLM fallback retain their models.\n\n",

          "end_line": 136,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n**(b)**, with these contracts:\n\n* **The merge is the confirmation.** A decision takes effect when the pull\n  request carrying it is merged by the maintainer, or by an agent on the\n  maintainer's explicit request in the conversation. A decision is any file\n  `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided`: an ADR under `docs/adr/`,\n  an ADR answer under `decisions/answers/`, the rule set\n  (`docs/governance/regelwerk.md`, `docs/governance/quality-gates.md`) and\n  `.claude/rules/`.\n* **No commit signing in Coding Harness, now or later.** No signers file, no\n  anchor commit, no key-loss recovery, no signature gate. The follow-up\n  signature change the interview planned is void.\n* **An agent records; it does not decide.** An agent may write a decision\n  file, recording only what the maintainer stated\n  (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), and never writes\n  an answer of its own as the maintainer's.\n* **A decision pull request says that it decides.** Its title is\n  `decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n  `decision`, and its body starts with the block from\n  `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`: what the merge decides, what\n  it confirms, the options and what follows. One decision per pull request;\n  up to three only when none can be accepted without the others. Every other\n  pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, which says on its\n  first lines that nothing is decided.\n* **An agent merges only on request, with the decision in view.** It\n  restates the decision block in the conversation and as a pull request\n  comment, stops if CI is red, never uses `--admin`, and merges with\n  `--match-head-commit`, so a branch that moved after the restatement is not\n  merged (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\").\n* **Claude Code asks before every merge command it recognises.** The ask\n  rules in `.claude/settings.json` come from one list\n  (`scripts/merge_guard.py`); the permission prompt appears right below the\n  restatement.\n* **The acceptance is recorded in the merge and nowhere else.** No agent\n  writes an approver's name or date for a merge that has not happened —\n  accepted is derived, not set (the idea of rule RB-M1). The gate\n  `adr-answers` holds existence and format only.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen: option (1), with the inference removed, the reverse direction held,\nand the whole gate carried by the kit with a day per repository — because an\nattribution per edit needs the claim where the edit is made, one rule is\neasier to hold than an explicit rule beside a guess, and a workflow rule that\nholds in one repository alone is not a rule of the workflow (Q-1 to Q-5).\n\n**What is decided**, in five points:\n\n1. A change claims, in the header of its own spec, every file under\n   `docs/adr/` it creates, changes or removes. A later change that amends an\n   ADR claims that amendment itself.\n2. An ADR edit belongs to the change of the measured work that claims it. A\n   change that does not claim the file is no owner of it, whatever else the\n   work touches. The owner owes five interview answers of the maintainer,\n   whatever its class and its date.\n3. An ADR edit that no change of the work claims is a finding that names the\n   remedy. Nothing infers an owner from the paths a diff touches or from an\n   ADR's text.\n4. For a feature begun after its repository adopted the gate, the answer \"yes\"\n   comes with at least one claimed ADR file, and the answer \"no\" with none.\n5. The interview gate travels with the kit as mechanism. Each repository\n   records the day it adopted the gate; a change begun on or before that day\n   is exempt from the class minimums and from point 4, never from points 2 and\n   3. Moving that day is a decision pull request.\n\n**How it holds from this change on:**\n\n* The claim is the spec header field `adr_files`; the gate\n  `interview-minimums` (`scripts/check_interview_minimums.py`) holds points 2\n  to 4.\n* The day stands in `decisions/adoption.yaml`, a file that stays in its\n  repository; this repository's day is 2026-10-08, the day it adopted the\n  gate, so no change here moves between stock and subject. The gate reads the\n  day through `scripts/adoption.py`, which any other gate can call with its\n  own id (bead coding-harness-wpv); without the record the gate does not\n  measure (exit 3).\n* The gate script, its test, the reader and the reader's test travel as\n  mechanism (`scripts/kit/manifest.yaml`); the record stays as stock. An\n  instance such as LakeSwitch receives them with its next pinned Coding\n  Harness release (bead coding-harness-dj9).\n\n**What this record does not fix.** The field's name, the record's name and\nform, the reader and the gate's messages are the change's design: they change\nin an ordinary change as long as the five points hold.\n\nThis record amends no D- or O-number. Amends the phase-1\n  routing of ADR 0007 and research purpose of ADR 0011; supersedes neither\n  whole ADR and amends no numbered D/O decision.\n* Review: maintainer chose the amended direction in the research-swarm\n  interview on 2026-10-14–18, Q-1–Q-14; acceptance is the future merge, with\n  no agent-written approval. The first unmerged\nslice used six broad topic pairs and free public researchers. The maintainer\namended that on 2026-10-15: finder first, smaller topics, three same-brief\nmodels per repository topic and a fixed report/scoring contract (Q-7).\nPi's free-model path was observed to return 403 FreeTierError by the\nmaintainer; Q-8 replaces it with OpenCode Go through Pi, Q-9 selects DeepSeek,\nMiMo and Qwen Flash for online topics. This draft relies on that recorded\nobservation, not a new live probe. Public-only context survives the provider\nchange (Q-3, Q-6, Q-8). Q-10 adds free models offered by Go itself, selected\nfrom a fresh Pi catalog each run, only to online topics alongside the Flash\ntrio; Zen stays excluded. The source was read at `6146fde` on 2026-10-16;\nthis draft neither probes the catalog nor claims live availability. The\nrepository runtime pin is now Pi 1.2.0 (ADR 0019). Q-11 (2026-10-17)\nrecords that Pi's fresh catalog has no tool-support field and selects a second\npublic source, models.dev, for tool_call and deprecated status. These dated\nobservations are the maintainer's recorded evidence, not measurements by this\ndrafting call; models.dev failure excludes free seats but retains the\nrequired ones. Q-12 (2026-10-18) replaces both fixed trios: on that day\n`qwen3.8-flash`, a fixed online member, could not be called (wire API not\nmeasured) while other Go models answered, so a fixed trio would end every\nrun incomplete. Q-14 (2026-10-18) makes the substitutes live as\nwell: a seat declares one preferred model, and a substitute comes from the\nadmitted Go models of the fresh catalog, cheapest first.           "end_line": 1506,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept; one retry after the configured pause, then the declared\n  fallback through Pi; at most three rounds (\"The spec review before the plan\n  card\").\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`. On every route it first refuses, before any model\n  starts, a refused class or a `bounded`, `feature` or `architectural` change\n  without a current spec review free of open `[AMBIGUITY]` rows.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuse",

          "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    # The class statement and the current spec review (bead coding-harness-ttic): one admission\n    # for every route, checked before a model starts; a spike reaches the existing checks.\n    admission = review_admission(root, change)\n    if admission.class_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.class_problem)\n    if admission.review_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.review_problem)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::House rules",
          "end_line": 95,
          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

nothing else changes.\n        error.partial_answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n        raise error\n    answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n    if not answer.strip():\n        raise fail(\"claude\", done, \"the answer is empty\", key)\n    return answer\n",

          "excerpt": "def repair(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4b and 6: Codex repairs every taken finding in one call, checked and committed by the runner.\n\n    The attempts are Codex, one fresh Codex repair attempt with the first one's diagnostics, and one\n    Sonnet 5.5 stage-1 fallback after two failed post-run checks; a failed call or a leak-check BLOCK\n    stops without a fallback (ADR 0017). The orchestrator decides taken or rejected and re-checks with\n    the loop's next round and `review`, a fresh read-only Codex session; the verb writes no\n    `Broke a test` and starts no review. Every selected row's `Origin` is checked before any call\n    or write, an older block's selected row included (bead coding-harness-3h96). A taken Status that\n    already names a fix in the old hand-written form (`; fixed by`, `; fixed:`, `; repaired by`)\n    refuses before any call.\n\n    A selected row whose `Where` names a path the checkpoint cannot commit is handed to the\n    orchestrator before any model call: the runner reports it with the reason `runner-held path`,\n    appends the dated hand-step listing to findings.md once, and leaves the row's Status and\n    `Broke a test` cells unchanged (bead coding-harness-0zhf). Every row held, the existing\n    checkpoint commits that listing and the run exits 0 with no model call; a mixed batch dispatches\n    only the committable rows, names the held ones in the commit body, and ignores answer lines that\n    mention them.\n    \"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else CODEX\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    record = read_record(change, root)\n    current = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n    resolved = resolve_finding_rows(record, current)\n    taken, waiting = repair_targets(ctx, record, current, resolved=resolved)\n    if waiting:\n        raise Refused(f\"rows are waiting for a decision ({', '.join(waiting)}); decide them first.\")\n    # Both checks share the resolver's current rows. The target check covers older selected\n    # rows too; the shared check retains its scope without re-admitting superseded history.\n    target_refusal = target_origin_refusal(record, current, resolved=resolved)\n    if target_refusal:\n        raise Refused(target_refusal)\n    refusal = origin_refusal(record, current, resolved=resolved)\n    if refusal:\n        raise Refused(refusal)\n    if not taken:\n        raise Refused(\"no row is taken; nothing to repair.\")\n    legacy = [row[0] for _, row in taken if legacy_completed(row[7])]\n    if legacy:\n        # A legacy marker may name a completed fix or merely occur in an unrepaired reason.\n        # Refuse without rewriting and explain both corrections (spec, criterion 7).\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"rows carry a taken status that already names a fix ({', '.join(legacy)}); book the hand repair \"\n            \"by replacing the Status with `fixed — tests/<path>::<function>` or \"\n            \"`fixed — not a test — <reason>` and setting the loop row's `Broke a test` mark, then run \"\n            \"repair again; if the row is not repaired yet, reword its reason so it names no fix instead \"\n            \"of marking it fixed.\"\n        )\n    # The waiting, origin and legacy refusals above bind every selected row before any row is\n    # classified or handed off (spec, criterion 9).\n    hand = repair_hand_rows(root, change, taken)\n    hand_ids = [row[0] for _, row, _ in hand]\n    handed = set(hand_ids)\n    eligible = [(place, row) for place, row in taken if row[0] not in handed]\n    ids = [row[0] for _, row in eligible]  # the commit subject names only the repaired rows\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n\n    # A row already listed with the same held paths in an earlier block of this findings.md is\n    # reported again ",

          "citation": "docs/adr/0019-repository-pinned-pi-and-contract-tests.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 87,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Repository-local npm install with real offline contracts\",\nbecause it separates the runner from global updates and makes the original\nisolation measurement repeatable on every proposed version change.\n\n1. `tools/pi/package.json` holds the exact Pi dependency; its npm lock records\n   the dependency graph and integrity values. `tools/pi/install.sh` uses\n   `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. No installed dependencies are committed.\n2. Every runner Pi path, including loop/probe and interactive-session preflight,\n   extension confirmation and dispatch, uses `tools/pi/pi`. The wrapper refuses\n   a missing or mismatched local install and never installs or falls back globally.\n3. `tools/pi/.node-version` holds the exact CI Node version. The wrapper refuses\n   another major locally; minor/patch moves within that major remain eligible\n   for the same contracts. Pi and Node changes are proposed in pull requests.\n4. The suite starts real pinned Pi with synthetic credentials and a loopback\n   model stand-in, locally and in CI. It holds reviewer tool declarations and\n   refusal, suppression of discovered extension/MCP startup and skill/prompt/theme\n   reads, context-file exclusion and scratch-agent separation from ambient auth\n   and command-valued model configuration, extension input/results, the production session\n   policy's foreign-read blocking, model-list table and Go/Zen provider address\n   and key mapping. Missing prerequisites fail rather than skip these contracts.\n5. This replaces the requirement to repeat a manual measurement alone when the\n   pin moves; the manual Pi 1.1.0 findings remain historical evidence. The normal\n   verification gates and real contracts must pass before a version move ships.\n6. Authentication boundaries stay as decided: scratch reviewer configuration\n   and Go key only in `OPENCODE_API_KEY`; interactive sessions sign in from the\n   maintainer's own Pi agent directory. No paid Zen endpoint is enabled here.\n\n",

Runs before the prompt check,\n    the call line and any call, in a scratch directory with no key: a Pi off\n    the pin sends nothing. The session verb calls it after its argument and\n    handover checks.\n    \"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        env = foreign_env({\"HOME\": tmp, \"PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR\": tmp})\n        try:\n            done = launch(\n                [str(PI_WRAPPER), \"--version\"],\n                Path(tmp),\n                env,\n                timeout=PI_VERSION_SECONDS,\n                limit=f\"the version check's limit of {PI_VERSION_SECONDS} seconds\",\n            )\n        except CallFailed as error:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"{PI_WRAPPER} could not be checked ({error}); it is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; no call starts.\"\n            ) from None\n    said = (done.stdout or \"\").strip()\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        # The wrapper's own refusal names the defect; its last lines travel with this one.\n        tail = \"\\n\".join((done.stderr or \"\").splitlines()[-5:])\n        detail = f\": {tail}\" if tail else \"\"\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"{PI_WRAPPER} --version ended {done.returncode}; it is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; \"\n            f\"no call starts{detail}.\"\n        )\n    if said != PI_VERSION:\n        raise Refused(f\"pi {said or 'printed nothing'} is not the pinned {PI_VERSION}; no call starts.\")\n",

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::House rules",
          "end_line": 95,
          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`.           "end_line": 85,
          "excerpt": "## Consequences\n\n- The scan covers launch only, with existing exclusions; later edits/prompts,\n  approved arbitrary shell code and UI model/agent changes are not scanned.\n  Another model re-enters through the runner.\n- This change approves no new endpoint, credential or review order; the\n  `opencode-go` declaration is ADR 0011's.\n- Initial support is macOS Terminal only, with no silent fallback.\n- The proof of the policy is weaker than OpenCode's read-back: a bug in the\n  extension that its tests miss is not seen at launch.\n- Only dangerous `bash` patterns ask; a command outside the list runs unasked.\n- `~/.pi/agent` may hold other providers' credentials, so a model switched\n  inside the session can leave the declared endpoint unscanned.\n- `.git/` stays writable for the session.\n- Bead coding-harness-0al (the OpenCode 2.x failure) is superseded: no\n  `opencode` call remains.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "# ADR 0011 — The review loop runs through OpenCode Go, and ADR 0007's reviewer list is amended\n\n* Status: accepted by the merge of the pull request that carries this file.\n  Until that merge, the pull request's state is the decision's state: open\n  is proposed, closed is rejected. Amends ADR 0007 (decisions 2 and 3);\n  supersedes no ADR.
